summary: This work demonstrates a cavity-based method for measuring qubit frequency noise by detecting photon loss induced by dressed dephasing in a high-Q superconducting cavity coupled to a transmon. Repeated mid-circuit qubit measurements with post-selection separate noise-induced photon loss from intrinsic cavity decay, enabling noise spectroscopy at frequencies inaccessible to conventional qubit-based methods.
motivation: Standard qubit-based noise spectroscopy methods are limited to frequencies below a few hundred megahertz and cannot operate during strong driving. Superconducting cavities with millisecond-scale lifetimes offer a complementary platform for precision sensing and can probe higher-frequency noise spectral windows.
method:
A single cavity photon is initialized in a niobium cavity (T$_1^c = 11.3$ ms) coupled to a transmon ($T_1^q = 71$ µs, $
u_q/2\pi = 3.8$ GHz, dispersive shift $\chi/2\pi = 31.7$ kHz) via cavity-qubit coupling $g/2\pi = 6.4$ MHz. Qubit frequency noise at detuning $\Delta/2\pi = 508$ MHz drives dressed dephasing that converts cavity photons to qubit excitations; repeated mid-circuit qubit measurements every 4.95 µs with post-selection on ground-state outcomes isolate the noise-induced loss rate $\kappa_{\mathrm{dd}}$ from intrinsic cavity decay $\kappa_0$ using Bayesian fitting.
result: With injected noise, the protocol extracts $\kappa_{\mathrm{dd}} = (5.3 \pm 0.1)$ ms$^{-1}$ corresponding to a frequency-noise PSD of $S_{\delta\omega}(\Delta) = 295 \times 10^3$ Hz$^2$/Hz, validated by independent Stark-shift calibration (346 $\times 10^3$ Hz$^2$/Hz). Without added noise, an upper bound of $\kappa_{\mathrm{dd}} < (0.3$ s$)^{-1}$ constrains the intrinsic noise PSD to $S_{\delta\omega}(\Delta) < 5 \times 10^3$ Hz$^2$/Hz at 508 MHz.
